programme: GLIS3, THRA, AEBP1 and USF2 form a convergent (not complexed) endocrine-metabolic regulatory axis: GLIS3 sits at the genetic junction of pancreatic-islet and thyroid development (its own target set includes INS and NEUROG3), THRA is the thyroid-hormone receptor that reads that signal into metabolic gene programmes, AEBP1 drives adipocyte/microglial lipid handling through APOE, CD36 and FABP4, and USF2 is an E-box factor whose target set (ACACA, ABCA1, GCGR, PKLR, DPP4) covers the same glucose/lipid handling genes. Together they read as regulators of insulin, thyroid hormone and lipid flux rather than a physical complex.
role_in_a: Insulin/lipid dysregulation is a well-worked axis in Alzheimer's disease (the 'type 3 diabetes' hypothesis); GLIS3 is directly tied here to type 2 diabetes risk loci overlapping AD risk, and AEBP1 is tied to microglial lipid/APOE handling and to dysregulated cortical expression in late-onset AD.
role_in_b: THRA carries the fibromyalgia side: resistance-to-thyroid-hormone patients present with the muscle pain and fatigue picture that gets diagnosed as fibromyalgia, making disordered thyroid-hormone signalling a documented route into fibromyalgia-like symptoms.
shared_axis: If GLIS3 (and its metabolic co-regulators AEBP1, USF2) sit upstream of the same insulin/lipid/thyroid endocrine circuit that THRA reads out downstream, then AD's lipid-metabolic vulnerability and fibromyalgia's thyroid-mimicry symptom profile are two tissue-specific readouts of one dysregulated endocrine-metabolic axis rather than independent processes.
reasoning: Each side of the axis is independently anchored by retrieved literature — GLIS3 and AEBP1 in Alzheimer's disease, THRA in a syndrome that mimics fibromyalgia — so the programme is nameable and partly placed in each disease. But no source states that AD and fibromyalgia share this axis together; that link is inference from parallel single-disease evidence, and USF2's place in the module rests on its known lipid/glucose regulon rather than on any retrieved paper, since the USF2-AD papers were judged off-target.
support: PMID 26499758 — links GLIS3 (via shared T2D GWAS loci) to Alzheimer's disease risk; PMID 37085326 — places GLIS3 in a genetic-moderation study of amyloid/cognition in Alzheimer's disease; PMID 41516171 — AEBP1 targeting shifts microglial phenotype relevant to Alzheimer's immunotherapy; PMID 38568322 — AEBP1 dysregulated in late-onset Alzheimer's disease cortex; PMID 37469961 — untreated resistance-to-thyroid-hormone (THRA) patients present with a fibromyalgia-like clinical picture.
how_to_falsify: In matched AD and fibromyalgia cohorts, measure fasting insulin/lipid panel and free T4/TSH alongside regulon activity (target-gene expression: INS/NEUROG3 for GLIS3, APOE/CD36/FABP4 for AEBP1, ABCA1/GCGR/PKLR for USF2, and THRA's thyroid-responsive targets). If metabolic-endocrine status does not track with these TFs' target expression in either disease's tissue, or if ChIP/eQTL data show these factors do not actually engage their listed targets in patient tissue, the shared-axis account fails.
caveats: Tissue pairing is blood|brain, so the AD and fibromyalgia networks being compared are not the same tissue; only 3 independent cohort pairs underlie the 32 patient-group comparisons, limiting independent replication. Fibromyalgia has essentially no direct literature or Open Targets signal for any of these 12 factors except THRA, so role_in_b rests on one paper describing a phenocopy syndrome, not a direct fibromyalgia mechanism study. The single-view factors (CREBBP, RFX3, RELB, OTX1, KLF16, FOXO4) and the tissue-generic removals (RELB, E2F2/3, NR4A3, ERG, FOXO4, STAT1, IRF8, GFI1, PRDM1, ELK3, STAT3) show that interferon/immune and cell-cycle regulators expected in a blood-brain comparison were deliberately screened out, so this account should not be read as an immune-axis story.
